title: The Faithful Lantern
premise: In 1871, in a river garrison town cut off each winter when the bridge closes, battlefield nurse Ulyana Pemberton has spent twelve years quietly recording the names of soldiers that official ledgers omit — men written out of history so their pensions and their crimes could vanish with them. When the bridge closes early and a wounded stranger arrives carrying proof that a decorated colonel massacred a village Ulyana once nursed through cholera, she recognizes him as Tomas, the boy she promised in peacetime to protect if war ever found him again. Sheltering an enemy of the Crown forces her to choose between the silences that have kept her household safe and the justice her ledger was always meant to deliver. The novel ends at spring thaw: Ulyana surrenders her twelve years of names to a magistrate willing to be disgraced, the colonel falls not by violence but by testimony, and Tomas — presumed dead so he can live — joins the found family she has built from everyone else the records forgot.
about_author: Edmund Halloran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing military hospital registers before turning to fiction. He writes from a farmhouse near the old river crossings that inspired his novels about the people history declined to count.

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Floorboard
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. On the last market day before winter, Ulyana tends the garrison infirmary and adds three more omitted names to her hidden ledger. We learn her rules: never copy, never explain, never let anyone see you counting. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine, the sense that her careful life is borrowed time.

chapters.title: What the Bridge Decides
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Floodwaters close the bridge weeks ahead of schedule, stranding travelers and sealing the town into itself. The garrison celebrates; Ulyana feels the trap closing. Emotional beat: claustrophobia disguised as festivity, the town becoming a sealed room.

chapters.title: A Man Pulled from the Reeds
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A half-drowned stranger is dragged from the river below the broken span — shot, fevered, and carrying oilcloth-wrapped papers. When she cuts away his coat she recognizes a scar she stitched herself, years ago, in a cholera tent. Emotional beat: recognition as vertigo; the past arriving bleeding on her table.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with a flashback to the peacetime promise made over a dying boy's cot. She realizes the man is Tomas, now grown, now declared enemy, and that her old vow has come due. Emotional beat: guilt and tenderness colliding; a promise made lightly proving heavier than any oath she swore to the Crown.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Toast
chapters.summary: Colonel Ashworth's POV. At the officers' winter ball, Ashworth toasts the season's 'clean books' while privately burning correspondence. He suspects papers went missing after the Vellin Creek action and orders the town searched. Emotional beat: polished menace; villainy as bookkeeping.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silences
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She hides Tomas in the disused fever ward behind the laundry, lying for the first time to her housekeeper Marta — and discovering Marta already knew and said nothing. Emotional beat: the shock of learning her found family has been protecting her all along.

chapters.title: The Papers Say Vellin Creek
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV, waking. He explains what he carried: muster rolls proving the colonel ordered a village burned and its dead struck from every record — the same erasure Ulyana has spent twelve years fighting. Emotional beat: two private griefs recognizing each other as one cause.

chapters.title: Searches and Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Soldiers ransack the infirmary while Marta runs interference with tea, lies, and a staged funeral for a nameless corpse. Emotional beat: courage performed as domesticity; the household becoming a conspiracy of kindness.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Carries Messages
chapters.summary: Pip's POV, an orphan errand-runner Ulyana feeds. Pip starts ferrying notes between the fever ward and a sympathetic magistrate's clerk, thrilled and terrified to matter. Emotional beat: a child discovering that being trusted is both gift and burden.

chapters.title: Ashworth Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Colonel Ashworth's POV. With the magistrate too ill to act, Ashworth declares martial powers for the winter and announces that anyone harboring the fugitive will hang with him. Emotional beat: lawful tyranny tightening; the law itself becoming the enemy.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost Her
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A long night inventorying her ledger, she confronts the names she failed to save and the ones she saved by staying silent — including one entry that could damn her own brother. Emotional beat: reckoning; survival revealed as a debt compounding interest.

chapters.title: Fever in the Fever Ward
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. His wound turns septic; Ulyana must fetch laudanum from the garrison stores under Ashworth's nose, trading a dangerous favor with a sergeant who wants his own name entered in her ledger. Emotional beat: desperation bartered honestly; mercy with a price tag.

chapters.title: The Sergeant's Name
chapters.summary: Sergeant Doyle's POV. Doyle, who helped burn Vellin Creek and has hated himself since, agrees to testify in exchange for being remembered truthfully rather than honorably. Emotional beat: a perpetrator choosing witness; shame transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Laundry Line
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pressured by a soldier's threat, Pip's friend lets slip that someone hidden is 'getting better.' Ashworth sets a watch on the infirmary. Emotional beat: innocence weaponized; guilt without malice.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Coat
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. To buy time, the household stages Tomas's death — the same nameless corpse from chapter eight buried under his papers' weight of rumor. Ashworth believes it, then doesn't. Emotional beat: grief performed as strategy; mourning a living man.

chapters.title: Ice on the River Road
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Too weak to stay and too hunted to remain, Tomas must cross the frozen river toward the magistrate's house with Pip guiding and Doyle covering their tracks. Emotional beat: flight as pilgrimage; the landscape hostile and holy at once.

chapters.title: Ashworth Offers a Bargain
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ashworth confronts Ulyana privately: hand over the papers and he'll bury Vellin Creek forever — and protect her brother's secret with it. Emotional beat: temptation sharpened to a scalpel; the price of silence stated aloud at last.

chapters.title: The Choice of Names
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In the novel's moral crux, she weighs her brother's safety against the village dead, and chooses — reading her entire ledger aloud to the recovering magistrate, brother included. Emotional beat: terrible liberation; justice chosen over safety, finally understanding what her silences were for.

chapters.title: Testimony by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Through one night, Ulyana, Tomas, Doyle, and Marta give sworn testimony while Ashworth's loyalists try to seize the courthouse. Pip holds the door. Emotional beat: climax as chorus; ordinary voices outweighing rank.

chapters.title: What the Colonel Burned Last
chapters.summary: Ashworth's POV. Cornered, Ashworth burns his final papers and nearly burns the courthouse, but Doyle stands between him and the witnesses. Arrested by his own officers, he demands to know which name undid him. Emotional beat: the fall of a man who mistook record-keeping for power.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The bridge reopens; the magistrate, disgraced but unbowed, forwards the testimony to the capital. Tomas is declared dead on paper so he can live free, and asks to stay anyway. Emotional beat: release after long constriction; spring as verdict.

chapters.title: The Faithful Lantern
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, closing. She begins a new ledger — not of omissions but of witnesses — and hangs a lantern in the infirmary window, the signal they agreed on for anyone else the records forgot. Emotional beat: resolution as continuation; found family keeping the light lit for the next arrival.
